verification: Every component below was read from src/index.ts (323 lines), src/app.jsx (854 lines), src/lib/api.js, public/index.html (31 lines), package.json and wrangler.json. Line references are exact.

maturityVocabulary.adequate: Works, minor gaps that do not block beta
maturityVocabulary.fragile: Works but a known defect makes it likely to break or mislead

components.name: Cloudflare Workers runtime
components.role: Hosts the app; serves static assets host-side and forwards everything else to the Durable Object
components.notes: html_handling=auto-trailing-slash + not_found_handling=single-page-application configured correctly for an SPA.

components.name: App Durable Object
components.role: Single DO class named App - acts as both the HTTP server and the stateful persistence unit. One instance per (space, branch).
components.entry: src/index.ts:4 export class App extends DurableObject
components.notes: Correct platform pattern - no export default {fetch}, no illegal DO bindings. Constructor does real work (initDb on every instantiation; seedDefaults only when SEED_DEMO_DATA=true), which is a latency and ordering concern.

components.name: Hono router
components.role: In-process HTTP router; 8 routes registered in the DO constructor
components.notes: No 404 fallback route - unknown paths fall through to the assets layer and return the SPA shell, which masks client-side routing errors.

components.name: SQLite storage (DO-attached)
components.role: Per-(space,branch) SQLite database via this.ctx.storage.sql. Two tables: todos (13 cols), lists (5 cols).
components.notes: Schema created idempotently (IF NOT EXISTS) - good. But: tags stored as JSON TEXT (not normalised), no indexes defined beyond PRIMARY KEY, no migration path, and no foreign key from todos.list_id to lists.id.

components.name: Static asset layer
components.role: Serves public/ host-side before any Worker invocation: the index.html shell plus the compiled bundles public/assets/app.js and public/assets/app.css
components.evidence: public/index.html (31 lines), public/assets/app.js + public/assets/app.css (build output, gitignored)
components.notes: public/assets/ is build output, not committed - a fresh clone serves a 404 page until 'npm run build' runs, so dev and CI must both build first. Still one HTML shell with no code splitting, but the heavy payload is now a separate cacheable file.

components.name: Single-file React SPA
components.role: One App() component holding all 24 useState hooks; all UI, data fetching, and timer logic in one scope
components.notes: No component decomposition, no router, no state management boundary. It is no longer an inline 40KB script transpiled at page load - esbuild compiles it ahead of time - but it is still one function holding everything, so every feature added increases coupling. This remains the main structural debt.

components.name: Client-side data access layer
components.role: One api() helper wraps every request and rejects on any non-2xx; 9 call sites (fetchTodos, fetchLists, fetchStats, handleCreateTodo, toggleComplete, togglePin, deleteTodo, incrementPomodoro, createList) report failure through fail() into a dismissible ErrorBanner with retry
components.entry: src/lib/api.js:47 api(); src/app.jsx:117 fail(); src/app.jsx:30 ErrorBanner
components.evidence: src/lib/api.js:45-81 (ApiError, describeError, api), src/app.jsx:117-124 (fail/clearError), 30-72 (ErrorBanner), 151-310 (call sites), 849 (banner rendered)
components.notes: Fixed 2026-10-17: a failed request is now visible instead of silently stale. api() rejects on non-2xx, surfaces the server's own error message, and mutations that lose typed input keep the form open. Still missing: loading states, request debounce (search fires per keystroke), optimistic updates, and abort on unmount. Relative ./api paths are correct for the preview prefix, which is a genuinely good call.

components.name: Build pipeline (esbuild + Tailwind CLI)
components.role: npm run build compiles src/app.jsx into public/assets/app.js (esbuild, IIFE) and src/tailwind.css into public/assets/app.css (Tailwind CLI). Supersedes COMP-008, COMP-009 and COMP-011.
components.evidence: package.json:6-8, tailwind.config.cjs, src/tailwind.css; CI builds then asserts both outputs in .github/workflows/ci.yml
components.notes: Removed 2026-10-17. The browser now does zero build work: no JSX transpile, no CSS JIT, and no third-party script executes with page privilege. React, react-dom and lucide-react are pinned npm packages bundled into app.js, so esm.sh is gone entirely. Remaining third-party surface is Google Fonts (COMP-012) only. 'npm run dev' and 'npm run deploy' both run the build first, so the two outputs cannot be missing by accident.

components.name: Custom design tokens
components.role: Brand colour scale as CSS custom properties plus fadeIn/scaleIn keyframes, compiled into app.css by the Tailwind CLI
components.notes: Clean token scale. Note the brand palette is defined TWICE - here as CSS vars and again in tailwind.config.cjs theme.extend.colors - so they can drift. It now compiles into app.css instead of being a separately linked stylesheet, which is why public/style.css is gone.

components.name: Web typography
components.role: Inter (sans) + JetBrains Mono (mono) loaded from Google Fonts with preconnect
components.notes: preconnect with crossorigin is correct. External font CSS can be blocked in privacy-strict regions, and there is no font-display:swap fallback guaranteeing text visibility.

components.name: Server-side seed data
components.role: Injects 4 lists and 4 sample tasks on first run when the lists table is empty, and only when SEED_DEMO_DATA=true
components.evidence: src/index.ts:237-238 (SEED_DEMO_DATA gate in the constructor), 273 (empty-table guard)
components.notes: Opt-in since 2026-10-17: wrangler.json sets SEED_DEMO_DATA=false so a real deployment starts with a clean slate, and .dev.vars.example shows how to switch it on locally. Guarded by an empty-table check so it is not destructive. Still runs in the constructor, so it is re-checked on every DO instantiation.

components.name: Configuration & typing
components.role: wrangler.json for deploy; env typed as any in the DO constructor
components.notes: env: any forfeits all binding type safety. Local overrides are now documented (.dev.vars.example, wrangler vars) but there is still no environment separation between dev and production, and no TypeScript config in the project itself (types come from the platform).

components.name: Quality assurance
components.role: Tests and typecheck gate (still absent) plus the CI pipeline that now exists
components.evidence: ci.yml runs the Worker bundle check, a docs-sync gate and seed validation on every push; 0 files match *test*/*spec*
components.notes: CI now gates every push and release.yml publishes a GitHub Release from CHANGELOG.md on a v* tag - but there are still no unit tests and no typecheck job, so none of the 30 features is regression-guarded and any refactor is an unverified gamble. maturity deliberately stays 'missing': G-QUAL-01 asks whether automated tests exist, and counting a pipeline without tests would make the checklist lie. This is still the single largest structural gap between alpha and beta.

components.name: Authentication & tenancy
components.role: Identity, access control, data isolation between users
components.evidence: grep for auth|bearer|token|session|cookie = only a string literal in an alert()
components.notes: Isolation currently relies entirely on the platform fact that one DO instance serves one deployment. That is single-tenant by architecture, not by access control - it protects a private deploy but cannot support a shared beta.

components.name: Hackathon routes module
components.role: Hono routes for hackathon CRUD, eligibility engine, and user profile. Registered in the App DO constructor.
components.notes: All SQL parameterised. Eligibility engine is a pure function — rules stored as JSON per hackathon.

components.name: Attachment routes module
components.role: Hono routes for attachment upload, list, download, and delete, scoped to a ticket (a hackathon or a todo). Screenshots are stored as BLOBs in the same SQLite database as the tickets.
components.notes: BLOB storage in SQLite — no size limit until the DO's 10GB cap. Route is /api/tickets/:id/attachments, with /api/todos/:id kept as a backwards-compatible alias. Images are immutable evidence of what a competition page showed.

components.name: Archive routes module
components.role: Wayback Machine CDX API adapter. Fetches archived snapshots, parses HTML for deadlines/prizes/rules, stores snapshots as attachments.
components.notes: Avoids scraping live platforms — the Wayback Machine archives are public and immutable. No ToS exposure.

components.name: Settings routes module
components.role: Configurable backend settings: storage backend (R2/S3/Azure), user profile, notification preferences, email/IMAP. Sensitive values obfuscated before storage.
components.notes: Obfuscation is XOR-based — prevents casual reading, not a substitute for real secret management. Documented as such.

components.name: Capacity planner module
components.role: Weekly available-hours template, daily digest with prioritised tasks, conflict detection, and weekly plan.
components.notes: Greedy assignment of tasks to available hours. The prioritisation score is urgency x 0.4 + prize x 0.3 + eligibility x 0.3.

components.name: JMAP email client
components.role: JMAP (RFC 8620/8621) client for JMAP-compatible email servers. Session discovery, batched API calls, email search, body retrieval, attachment download.
components.notes: JSON-based alternative to IMAP — no MIME parsing, stateless, push-capable. The open standard the French government uses via La Suite numerique.

components.name: Inbox routes module
components.role: Receives parsed emails from the Cloudflare Email Worker, stores them as inbox items, and links them to hackathon tickets by content matching on the email subject against hackathon names.
components.notes: Stores extracted metadata only, not raw email — data minimisation per GDPR. Links by content first (subject vs hackathon name) so two competitions on the same platform stay distinguishable; falls back to the platform only when it holds exactly one entry, and refuses to guess otherwise.

components.name: Cloudflare Email Worker
components.role: Separate Worker that receives inbound mail via Cloudflare Email Routing, parses it with postal-mime, and POSTs the extracted data to the taskmaster inbox API.
components.entry: scripts/email_worker.ts:1 export default { async email(message, env, ctx) }
components.notes: Deployed separately from the main Worker — it is an email handler, not an HTTP handler. postal-mime is MIT licensed.

components.name: React error boundary
components.role: Catches render errors in the component tree and shows a recoverable fallback instead of a blank page.
components.notes: The one thing a single-component crash must not take down is the whole app.

dataFlow: Hono [COMP-003] -> SQL exec on DO storage [COMP-004]
DO [COMP-002] persists via ctx.storage.sql, surviving redeploys
Static assets [COMP-005] served host-side; only unmatched requests reach the DO
Build [COMP-017] writes public/assets/app.js and app.css before dev, CI and deploy
Google Fonts [COMP-012] is the only third-party load remaining at page view

structuralDebt: COMP-006 - 800 lines in one component, no decomposition (was 821; same shape)
COMP-015/COMP-016 - no tests and no auth
summary.assessment: The architecture is coherent and uses the platform correctly - the DO/SQLite/Hono pattern is idiomatic and the asset routing is right. The build step that used to be the third absence arrived on 2026-10-17: the browser no longer transpiles JSX or JITs CSS, and every CDN script except Google Fonts is gone. What holds it at alpha now is two absences (auth, tests) plus a single-component frontend that cannot absorb much more growth without decomposition.
